bug_semantics: A malicious Composer repository can put shell metacharacters after the @ delimiter in a package's Perforce source reference. PerforceDownloader extracts that suffix and passes it to Perforce::syncCodeBase(), which concatenates it into a string command as @<sourceReference> and gives the string to ProcessExecutor. The shell interprets the metacharacters before p4 is launched, so installing or updating from source can execute arbitrary commands even when Perforce itself is absent.
flaw_origin: Commit dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea is the smallest commit that created the advisory's source-reference-to-shell path: it replaced getPrettyVersion() with getLabelFromSourceReference($ref), added extraction of the substring after @ from PackageInterface::getSourceReference(), and passed that value to syncCodeBase(), where it was appended without escaping. Its direct parent already had generic string command construction using a pretty-version label, but did not derive the appended value from sourceReference; the exact CVE-2026-40261 source-reference mechanism is absent there.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea shows author and committer Clark Stuth <clarkstuth@gmail.com>; the complete commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory bundle for GHSA-gqw4-4w2p-838q states that malicious package metadata reaches Perforce::syncCodeBase(), that shell metacharacters in sourceReference permit arbitrary command execution, and that the fixed releases are 2.2.27 and 2.9.6; advisory URL: https://github.com/composer/composer/security/advisories/GHSA-gqw4-4w2p-838q.

The CVE.org API record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-40261 is PUBLISHED and independently names the same syncCodeBase source-reference concatenation, affected ranges >=1.0.0,<2.2.27 and >=2.3.0,<2.9.6, and fixed releases 2.2.27/2.9.6.

git diff 3a3661a0b3ff307e5084fa4846c6e72feb904022 dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea -- src/Composer/Downloader/PerforceDownloader.php src/Composer/Util/Perforce.php shows one atomic data-flow change: doDownload() changes from $package->getPrettyVersion() to getLabelFromSourceReference($package->getSourceReference()), adds the @-suffix extractor, and passes that value to syncCodeBase(), which concatenates '@' . $sourceReference into the command string.

Direct parent-tree verification at 3a3661a0b3ff307e5084fa4846c6e72feb904022 shows PerforceDownloader.php lines 31-32 obtaining sourceReference only for $ref while the value passed to syncCodeBase() is getPrettyVersion(); Perforce.php lines 312-319 accept $label. The sourceReference-to-sync-shell path introduced by dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea is therefore absent in the immediate parent.

git cat-file commit dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea verifies a single parent 3a3661a0b3ff307e5084fa4846c6e72feb904022, author/committer Clark Stuth <clarkstuth@gmail.com>, subject 'fixed perforce to reference labels instead of invalid tags', and no AI-related trailer; this is an ordinary atomic commit, not a squash aggregate requiring decomposition.

git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea is an ancestor of tags 1.0.0, 2.2.26, 2.2.27, 2.9.5, and 2.9.6. Tag-tree inspection shows the unescaped append at src/Composer/Util/Perforce.php:447 in 2.2.26 and :354 in 2.9.5, matching the affected upper boundaries.

Mainline commit 91f077050c13e49e22554b991c81378ce8b5ee16 directly changes syncCodeBase() from appending raw '@' . $sourceReference to ProcessExecutor::escape('@' . $sourceReference); it is absent from 2.9.5 and is an ancestor of 2.9.6. LTS commit 3448a8f255f14161ed8b10a1420e5c29f2637cfb applies the equivalent one-line direct fix, is absent from 2.2.26, and is an ancestor of 2.2.27.

Commit 4fcc13d428f28479b01f757341aadd625412b454, subject 'Convert perforce util to use array process args to avoid injections', replaces string command assembly with argument arrays and is an ancestor of 2.9.6; tag 2.9.6 has syncCodeBase() append sourceReference as a separate argv element. Release boundary: https://github.com/composer/composer/releases/tag/2.9.6.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and published: repository-controlled package metadata supplies a Perforce source reference, doInstall/doDownload extracts its @ suffix, and syncCodeBase() appends that untrusted suffix to a shell-interpreted command. History tracing distinguishes the pre-existing generic label concatenation from the advisory's exact taint source: dd1fd0e306dbad073fa8b32c0b23eea52ada8dea is the first commit that routes getSourceReference() into that sink, while direct parent 3a3661a0b3ff307e5084fa4846c6e72feb904022 routes getPrettyVersion() instead. The BIC predates tag 1.0.0 and persists in both vulnerable boundary tags. Mainline direct fix 91f077050c13e49e22554b991c81378ce8b5ee16 escapes the source-reference argument, LTS commit 3448a8f255f14161ed8b10a1420e5c29f2637cfb applies the same direct fix, and 4fcc13d428f28479b01f757341aadd625412b454 completes the mainline conversion to argv arrays; the fixed tags contain the appropriate fixes. The BIC object's author, committer, and complete message contain no AI marker, so the BIC-only attribution rule yields NOT_AI regardless of any AI signals elsewhere in the repository.
